{{< include ../exercise-header.qmd >}}


::: {#exr-arm-hold-hamper}
Write `0.00056` in scientific notation. The expected answer is `5.6e-4`.

Write `7.2e5` in ordinary decimal notation. The expected answer is `720,000`.

Two positive quantities have scientific-notation exponents 4 and 7. By how many orders of magnitude do their sizes differ, approximately? The expected answer is 3.

MAYBE MOVE THIS TO AN EXERCISE: Make up two scientific notation numbers, one with and exponent of 4 and the other an exponent of 7. Your job is to select mantissas that

a. will make the order of magnitude difference almost exactly 3.

b. will make the order of magnitude difference practically 4.

c. will make the order of magnitude difference practically 2.

d. Are there mantissas in the conventional format (with one digit to the left of decimal point) that can make the order of magnitude 5? (Hint: Think about the signs.)

e. Are there mantissas in the conventional format (with one digit to the left of decimal point) that can make the order of magnitude 6?

:::
